summary: Edge connection-hold flood from long-lived keepalive clients causing 5xx spike and runtime CPU pressure for dedicated tenant
description:
Issue summary:
During the customer tenant's steady-state traffic window (03/12 07:15–08:45 UTC) we observed an abrupt rise in 5xx rates originating at the API gateway layer for BeaconHealth Analytics (dedicated tenant). Error rate climbed from baseline ~0.2% to a peak of 6.3% for their routes and correlated with elevated CPU utilization on several serving-runtime pods pinned to the tenant.

Impact:
- Multiple customer API routes returned 5xx (predominantly 502/503) for ~90 minutes, affecting live clinical scoring and chat features.
- Observed increased tail latency and client-visible stream disconnects.
- Customer reported degraded SLA and raised a high-priority support case.

Environment:
- Dedicated tenant: BeaconHealth Analytics, prod-us-east, routing through edge-proxy cluster ep-us-1
- API Gateway version: apigw-3.7.1
- Edge proxy: envoy-1.26-custom
- Serving runtime image: redwood-runtime:2026-03-05-prod

Observed symptoms / logs:
- Edge accept-queue length increased prior to error wave: accept_queue_depth ep-us-1 peaked at 11k connections.
- Large number of long-lived keepalive connections from a small set of client IPs (slow-client pattern) holding multipath HTTP/2 streams in half-open state.
- Runtime pods serving the tenant logged frequent "worker-saturated" and "kv-cache-rate-limit-ejection" messages followed by "watchdog-reset" on high CPU.
- API gateway returned 502/503 to callers when upstream runtime stopped responding to new requests.
- Netstat/metrics show high socket count with many connections in CLOSE_WAIT / HALF_OPEN for the tenant's routed IPs.

Hypothesis:
- A small subset of clients are performing connection-holding/keepalive behavior (similar to slowloris), preventing the edge from reusing sockets efficiently and causing accept-queue growth. This in turn amplifies head-of-line blocking and creates load on specific runtime workers (KV cache hot-sharding + continuous batching starvation), pushing CPU to saturation and triggering watchdog restarts leading to 5xx responses.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Route a burst of long-lived HTTP/2 keepalive connections from ~200 clients that hold idle streams while occasionally sending small requests.
2) Maintain these connections over several minutes while the normal traffic mix continues.
3) Observe accept queue growth at edge-proxy and elevated runtime CPU for tenant-scoped workers.
4) Confirm increase in 502/503 responses and streaming session disconnects for routes mapped to the tenant.
logs: 2026-03-12T07:27:17Z edge-proxy envoy WARNING: many half_open streams from 34.85.102.11/32
2026-03-12T07:31:02Z runtime[beacon-rt-3] ERROR: worker-saturated cpu=98% pid=2427 msg=watchdog-reset
investigation_notes:
Initial triage performed by SRE shows concentrated socket-hold behavior from a small set of customer IPs. Edge metrics indicate accept-queue became the bottleneck before runtime CPU throttling. We reproduced a FIFO starvation pattern in a local simulation by holding HTTP/2 streams open while issuing infrequent requests; this caused per-worker batch queues to back up and CPU utilization to rise due to retry/spin loops.

We correlated the tenant's request logs with the IP ranges in the customer's environment; BeaconHealth confirmed a third-party data-collector update rolled out earlier that morning which altered clients to keep connections open for longer to reduce TLS handshakes. This change inadvertently increased connection concurrency.

Temporary mitigations trialed:
- Enabled per-tenant connection rate-limiter on the edge for a subset of routes (reduced connection growth by ~60%).
- Adjusted accept queue high-water mark alerting and increased ephemeral worker pool by +2 for the tenant's shard.
Both actions reduced immediate 5xx rate but did not fully eliminate intermittent watchdog resets on the runtime.
comments: 2026-03-12 08:02 - Riley Chen: Assigned. Collecting pcap from edge-proxy nodes and will correlate with runtime metrics. Asked SRE to preserve node state and not recycle pods.

2026-03-12 08:15 - SRE (Jordan Mills): Captured live tcpdump; saw many streams with only keepalive frames for >120s. Suspect client-side change. Also bumped ephemeral workers by 2 on beacon shard; initial 10min window shows error rate drop to 2.1%.

2026-03-12 09:05 - Customer (BeaconHealth - DevOps, Maria Lopez): We pushed an update at 06:50 UTC to the telemetry agent — rolling it back now and will confirm if connections drop. Appreciate the rapid response.

2026-03-12 09:32 - Riley Chen: After rollback by customer, connection counts from identified IPs dropped ~85% and 5xx rates returned near baseline. Keeping this ticket open to perform follow-up hardening and a post-incident writeup.

2026-03-13 11:20 - Product Ops (Evan Park): Recommend adding an edge-level per-tenant idle-stream timeout and an option for auto-fallback to lightweight proxy path under accept-queue pressure. Logged feature request INT-3321.
resolution_notes:
Workaround applied: Coordinated with BeaconHealth to roll back the telemetry agent change; enabled per-tenant connection rate-limiting temporarily and increased ephemeral worker count for the affected shard. Result: 5xx rates dropped from 6.3% peak to ~0.25% baseline within 20 minutes.

Permanent actions planned:
- Implement edge idle-stream timeout and per-route max idle streams (Engineering ticket INT-3321).
- Add heuristic detection for keepalive-dominant clients with automated rate-limiting and alerts (SRE runbook update linked).
- Add tenant-level dashboarding for connection-age distribution to surface similar regressions earlier.

Follow-up owner: Riley Chen. Target for mitigation rollout: 2026-04-02. Postmortem scheduled in Confluence and will be attached when complete.
customer_impact_summary: Tenant experienced degraded availability across chat and scoring endpoints for approximately 90 minutes. Root cause traced to a client-side change that increased long-lived keepalive connections; amplification at edge caused runtime worker saturation and watchdog resets yielding 5xx responses. Immediate remediation reduced customer impact; permanent mitigations planned.
next_steps: 1) Engineering to scope and implement edge idle-stream timeout (INT-3321).
2) SRE to add automated detection and alerting on rising connection-age percentiles per tenant.
3) Customer success to confirm BeaconHealth will adopt staggered rollouts for agent updates and add limits on client keepalive behavior.
4) Postmortem writeup and runbook updates to be created by 2026-03-20.
